skill.name: firefox-browser
skill.description: Automate a real Firefox browser through a local command bridge, including tab management, page inspection, form input, screenshots, and authenticated sessions.
skill.summary: Automate real Firefox sessions through a local browser command bridge.
skill.author: 1jehuang

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting false positives, not Ruby shell backtick execution. The real risk is semantic: the skill controls an authenticated Firefox session, can capture screenshots and page content, can run arbitrary page JavaScript, and can use a Bitwarden vault for autonomous login.

remediation.issue: Authenticated browser control has broad account-action scope.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before clicks, form submissions, purchases, account changes, or actions on authenticated pages.

remediation.issue: Credential vault automation can fill and submit secrets without a user present.
remediation.suggestion: Disable automatic submission by default, require per-domain approval, and prevent credential values from being exposed to page content or logs.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary JavaScript evaluation can read private page state.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict evaluate to trusted tasks, add allowlists for safe read-only scripts, and require approval for pageWorld execution.

remediation.issue: Screenshots and page extraction can reveal sensitive information.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before capture, avoid saving screenshots unless requested, and redact secrets from logs and examples.

content.value_statement: Manual browser tasks are slow when pages require real cookies, sessions, and interactive forms. This skill lets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code drive a local Firefox session through a browser bridge.
actual_capabilities: Lists open Firefox tabs and switches the active tab for a task.
Creates new tabs or windows and navigates to requested URLs.
Extracts page content in text, HTML, or annotated interactive formats.
Clicks elements, types text, fills forms, scrolls pages, and waits for UI changes.
Captures visible-page screenshots and verifies form state from the browser.
Supports Bitwarden-assisted login and page JavaScript evaluation when available.
limitations: Requires Firefox, the bridge extension, and the browser command to be installed locally.
Uses the user's real browser profile, so actions may affect live accounts.
Cannot guarantee website compatibility across every authentication flow or dynamic UI.
Sensitive actions need human review because screenshots, cookies, and credentials may be involved.

use_cases.title: Check Account Pages
use_cases.description: Open authenticated pages, read visible content, and summarize status without requiring a separate headless login.

use_cases.title: Test Web Forms
use_cases.description: Fill forms, verify validation messages, and inspect selected states in real Firefox sessions.

use_cases.title: Compare Web Information
use_cases.description: Open multiple sites or tabs, collect page text, and compare visible details across sources.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Current Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for understanding the active tab.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use firefox-browser to list my open tabs, select the active work tab, and summarize the visible page content.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Simple Form
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for controlled page interaction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use firefox-browser to open the form page I provide, identify the fields, fill the draft values, and stop before submitting.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Authenticated Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task involving a logged-in session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use firefox-browser to open the authenticated dashboard, read the relevant status fields, and ask before making any account changes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multiple Paths
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task using isolated tabs or forks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use firefox-browser to test two navigation paths in separate tabs, compare the outcomes, and close the unused path after review.

output_examples.input: Inspect the active tab and tell me what actions are available.
output_examples.output: The page shows a product detail view with price, quantity, cart, and review controls. Available actions include search, add to cart, select quantity, and open reviews.

output_examples.input: Check whether the profile form is ready to submit.
output_examples.output: The name and email fields are filled, the country selector is set, and the required consent box is unchecked. The form is not ready to submit.

output_examples.input: Compare the same item across two shopping pages.
output_examples.output: The first page lists a lower base price, while the second page includes faster shipping. Both pages show the item as available.

best_practices: Start each task by listing tabs and selecting a dedicated tab or window.
Use annotated content before clicking so selectors match the visible page.
Ask for confirmation before submitting forms, using saved credentials, or changing account data.
anti_patterns: Do not run purchases, payments, or account changes without explicit user approval.
Do not save screenshots or page content that contains secrets unless the user requested it.
Do not use arbitrary page JavaScript when a safer built-in browser action is sufficient.

faq.question: Does this use my real Firefox browser?
faq.answer: Yes. It controls a local Firefox session, including existing cookies and logged-in pages.

faq.question: Can it work with authenticated websites?
faq.answer: Yes, if the site is already logged in or the configured vault login flow is available.

faq.question: Can it take screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. It can capture the visible browser area, which may include sensitive page data.

faq.question: Does it require a local setup?
faq.answer: Yes. Firefox, the bridge extension, and the browser command must be available on the machine.

faq.question: Can it submit forms automatically?
faq.answer: The documented actions support form filling and submission, but sensitive submissions should require confirmation.

faq.question: Is it safe for financial or account administration tasks?
faq.answer: Use caution. The skill can act inside real accounts, so approval should be required before irreversible actions.
